architecture: hub + secondary-hub, same pattern as West of England (Bristol Temple Meads/Bath Spa) and Solent (Portsmouth Harbour/Portsmouth & Southsea), reused here — NOT full flat Option A. Reading (RDG) is the hub lock: single flat board, three operators (GWR/CrossCountry/SWR), no internal doNotGroup (report line 36 explicitly rules out multi-operator platform mixing). Oxford (OXF) is the secondary hub, but UNLIKE Bath Spa/Portsmouth & Southsea it needs an internal doNotGroup split: GWR main line and Chiltern Railways' Marylebone branch sit on separate platforms/infrastructure at Oxford and require separate boarding logic per operator (report line 37, 56, C2/C3 point 4/6). See direction-model-memo.md before wiring an adapter.
agency: National Rail (Darwin/OpenLDBWS) — Great Western Railway (dominant, Reading + Oxford main line), CrossCountry (through-running at Reading), Chiltern Railways (Oxford/Banbury, Marylebone branch), South Western Railway (through-running at Westbury boundary)

scopeNote: National Rail only (GWR, CrossCountry, Chiltern Railways, South Western Railway through-running) at Reading and Oxford, plus surrounding regional/through-running stations (Swindon, Banbury, Westbury, Henley-on-Thames, Didcot Parkway). No buses, no light rail, no trams, no Elizabeth Line in v1 scope (TfL Elizabeth Line also serves Reading but is a separate mode/operator, out-mode per report point 7). No Eurostar, no sleeper services named in this report's scope.
notes: D1 oracle is docs/thames-valley-d1/oracle-clash-report.md only. No product lib/cities/thames-valley/ exists yet. Not generated from GTFS. No stopIds in this file.

ARCHITECTURE: hub + secondary-hub (Reading hub-lock, Oxford secondary), same shape West of England and Solent already used. UNLIKE those regions' secondary hubs, Oxford needs doNotGroup: true internally (GWR main line vs Chiltern Marylebone branch, separate platforms/infrastructure). Reading itself does NOT need doNotGroup (report line 36: no multi-operator platform mixing, standard flat board applies despite three operators). See direction-model-memo.md.

Modes v1: National Rail heavy rail only. No light rail, no metro, no buses, no Elizabeth Line (report C2/C3 point 7 — TfL Elizabeth Line calls at Reading but is a separate mode/operator, out of v1 scope).

National Rail has NO static GTFS publication from NRE directly (Darwin is realtime-only, SOAP API). Transitland republishes a derived GTFS (CC-BY-2.0 UK, no key required) as a reference-only schedule source, not pulled to derive this catalog. Same open product-architecture question as every prior UK NR region: does Next Train support a Darwin-only next-train model, or does it need a GTFS base layer? Not resolved in this pack — see coverageGaps and jim-handoff.md.

CRS codes below (RDG, OXF, SWI, BAN, WSB, HEY, DID) are carried from the oracle report's station-name table and are NOT verified against a live GTFS dump or Darwin response. crsVerified: false throughout. Confirm before adapter wiring.

No 'lines' array is provided for either hub — no printed route/line map exists for National Rail in the oracle report; Darwin is a per-station real-time departure-board product. See direction-model-memo.md for the destination+operator model recommended instead of line+terminus.

City lands as 'Coming Soon' (status stays planned; there is no separate coming-soon enum value in registry.js) until National Rail is unblocked (DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN), same as every other UK National Rail region.

SKIP RISK — Chiltern Railways operator transition: Chiltern moves from Arriva to DfT Operator on 20 September 2026 (report skip risk 3, per March 2026 infrastructure update). Not a blocker, but a timing flag for whoever wires this adapter after that date — verify Darwin correctly attributes Chiltern services and that any operator/agency mapping reflects the new structure post-transition.

License: OGL 2.0 baseline with NRE amendments for Darwin. Confidence 'unclear' on third-party rider redistribution — same open item as every other UK National Rail region. National Rail static GTFS (Transitland) is CC-BY-2.0 UK, confidence 'clear', reference-only.

Boundary consistency checked against the two named adjacent regions' finished packs (per dispatch instruction, not general cross-city context reading): Westbury already flagged as a Thames Valley/Solent boundary in docs/west-of-england-d1/published-network.json (throughRunningOnly list) and independently in docs/solent-d1/published-network.json (boundaryThroughRunning list). Paddington (GWR London terminus) is built as a stationGroup in docs/london-se-national-rail-d1/published-network.json with a boundaryNote naming West of England (not Thames Valley) as the corridor continuation — Thames Valley's own GWR services to/from Reading/Oxford originate at that same Paddington, which is NOT a Thames Valley station and is not built here. Marylebone (Chiltern's London terminus) is NOT built in london-se-national-rail's pack either (sits in that pack's notBuilt.secondary-termini list) — no double-build conflict exists today for either London terminus; flagged for D2 if either region later promotes its terminus to a built stationGroup.

No docs/united-kingdom-ledger.md exists yet (checked before starting this pack; none found in docs/). docs/country-lane.md names the UK ledger retrofit as required before the next NR region — this is another NR region shipped without it. This pack proceeds on the oracle report alone per the dispatch instruction; the Westbury/Paddington/Marylebone boundary facts recorded here should migrate into that ledger once it exists rather than being re-derived by future regions.

stationGroups.name: Reading
stationGroups.class: Hub lock — principal rail terminus and interchange for Thames Valley; 15 platforms, busiest station in Berkshire and third busiest in South East England outside London (report line 15). GWR Paddington services, Bristol/Bath connections, CrossCountry long-distance, SWR through-running from Solent. No multi-operator platform mixing (unlike London Bridge/Liverpool Street in london-se-national-rail) — boards must show all three operators but as one flat destination+operator list (report line 36, C2/C3 point 4).
stationGroups.role: hub lock, single lock-point and primary interchange

stationGroups.name: Oxford
stationGroups.doNotGroupReason: Two operators on different platforms and different infrastructure at one physical station — GWR main line (London/Reading/Bristol direction) vs Chiltern Railways (Marylebone branch). Report line 16, 37, 56, C2/C3 point 4/6: 'separate boarding logic required per operator... Two separate operators on different infrastructure. Boards must show both.' Not a merge into one flat board.
stationGroups.class: Hub secondary — Oxford city station; direct service to Reading (22-32 min frequency, report line 16). GWR regional connections to London/Reading/Bristol direction; Chiltern Railways services to London Marylebone. Regional through-hub for north-south routing (GWR line) and east-west routing (Chiltern line).
stationGroups.role: secondary hub, subordinate to Reading on the same corridor (unlike Solent's genuinely-independent Southampton/Portsmouth hubs)

throughRunningOnly.name: Swindon
throughRunningOnly.class: GWR main-line through-running point. National Rail only; GWR regional/intercity London-Bristol-Penzance continue through. Oxford/Banbury to Swindon via GWR line; no regional split at this station. Upstream of the Westbury boundary — not shared with West of England or Solent (report line 17).

throughRunningOnly.name: Banbury
throughRunningOnly.class: Through-running point, Chiltern main line + GWR Oxford branch. Chiltern from Marylebone via Oxford; GWR from Paddington via Oxford-Banbury to Birmingham. Two separate TOC operations on separate infrastructure at the same town, but not a hub candidate at D1 — not built as a stationGroup; proposed doNotGroup only if ever promoted (report line 18, 38).

throughRunningOnly.name: Westbury
throughRunningOnly.class: Through-running point, boundary to West of England / Solent regions. GWR services to Reading/Oxford (Thames Valley) and South Western Railway services to Southampton/Portsmouth (Solent) call at the same platform but operate separate franchises. Not a merge within Thames Valley — de-duplicate at D2. Already flagged reciprocally in both docs/west-of-england-d1/published-network.json and docs/solent-d1/published-network.json (report line 19, 39, 76).

throughRunningOnly.name: Henley-on-Thames
throughRunningOnly.class: Regional station on GWR branch line. Single operator (GWR). No through-running to other regions (report line 20).

throughRunningOnly.name: Didcot Parkway
throughRunningOnly.class: GWR main-line station, east of Oxford. Connection point for Cotswold Line (west to Hereford/Worcestershire); main line continues to Reading. Served by GWR regional only; no separate operators (report line 21).

boundaryThroughRunning.name: Westbury
boundaryThroughRunning.class: GWR (Reading/Oxford direction) and SWR (Southampton/Portsmouth direction) cross here. Already flagged as a boundary in docs/west-of-england-d1/published-network.json and docs/solent-d1/published-network.json. Not a merge; not a Thames Valley stationGroup.

boundaryThroughRunning.name: London Paddington
boundaryThroughRunning.crsSource: Not given by the Thames Valley oracle report (which never names Paddington); carried from docs/london-se-national-rail-d1/published-network.json's already-built paddington stationGroup, not independently sourced by this pack.
boundaryThroughRunning.class: GWR London terminus; Thames Valley's GWR services (Reading, Oxford) originate here, but Paddington itself is part of London & South East National Rail's catalog (already built as a stationGroup there, boundaryNote naming West of England as the westward continuation). Not a Thames Valley station, not built here.

No double-build conflict today; flagged for D2 if either region later promotes it.
